summary: This is a config-gated port of an already-measured, already-correct kernel onto the one shape where it won (sliding decode_1: 13.51 vs 16.56 us, about 18%). Every other shape stays byte-identical to master, so a single run is attributable per shape and needs no companion. The real risk is ordering against the running fa3-window-trimmed-page-table, not interpretability.
justification: The mechanism is plausible and measured, not inferred. At sliding decode_1 the shape is pure launch and latency (SoL 0.1 us). The master path is pre-attention, prepare_varlen_num_blocks, the FA3 main kernel, combine and rms_norm_gate. FINDINGS profiles it at FA3 8.2 us, combine 2.5 us and prepare 1.8 us, 16.3 us reported, and bfb7bac's own run has 16.56 us. The fused kernel's one launch measured 13.51 us on this exact shape (sliding-single-launch-fused-attention result.json). That run was built on fused-preattention-triton, whose sliding path is identical to master's: all three later landings touch only window == 0, so the old A/B carries over directly. The arithmetic is consistent with TASK weights. The decode_1 load is about 46*16.56 + 16*28.1 = 1211 us; saving 46*3.05 = 140 us is about 11.6% on that load, so roughly 1.9% on the 6-load geomean (1.269x to about 1.293x). Expected directions (faster on the one shape, same elsewhere) follow from the predicate (window and batch == 1 and q_len == 1, config only). Weakest link: the headline gain of about 1.9% sits just above the judge's +/-1.5% CI and inside the 1.5-2.5% run-to-run drift in LESSONS. As with batch-gate, the classifier may call it neutral even if it works, so judge it on the sliding decode_1 row (its paired ratio against SGLang and the fused kernel's top_kernels time of about 10.2 us) and on the other 11 rows staying flat. Second weakest: the 13.5 us comes from one run; Triton times reproduce within about 1%, so it is likely to hold. The S=16 in-kernel ticket combine adds no extra launch, which keeps the fused kernel's latency lower at B=1.
confounders: fa3-window-trimmed-page-table (running, not landed): it targets the same sliding FA3 path. If it gains at sliding decode_1 (it shrinks FA3's prepare and combine work and its split count, about 4.3 us of the 16.3), this hypothesis's margin against the new master shrinks or vanishes, because the gate bypasses FA3 entirely at that shape. Either claim this on master after that run harvests, or compare its decode_1 sliding row against whichever master it will be promoted onto.

fused-preattention-triton (landed): not a confounder for the measurement. The gated path replaces _pre_attention_kernel plus FA3 plus rms_norm_gate wholesale at that one shape, so the comparison is fused kernel versus master's full chain, which is exactly the decision. Every other shape still uses it unchanged.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing, paired-heads-launch-cleanup, paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate (landed): full layers only (window == 0); disjoint from the gated shape. The port must not disturb kernel_fn's paired branch: the early return sits before any paired logic, so it cannot.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is a config-only early return that affects exactly one scored shape, and the other 11 shapes run master's code byte for byte. So a gain or a loss on sliding decode_1 can only come from the swapped path, and the flat shapes serve as the in-run drift control. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not disambiguate anything: none of them touches the gated shape's path. A control isolating a sub-change (for example fused attention without the in-kernel combine) would be a new design question, not something needed to read this run. The one real dependency is the running fa3-window-trimmed-page-table. That is a sequencing question: dispatch after it harvests, or rebase onto the new master if it lands. It is not an A/B companion.
rules_flags: Precision: the fused path keeps queries in bf16, after the qk_scale_factor, as the reference does. That is finer than FP8 E4M3 and allowed ('no coarser'). P goes to bf16 for the PV dot; the KV cache stays E4M3 and is dequantized via the scales. All 16 tests passed with this kernel before.

Caching: _COUNTERS is keyed on (batch, hkv, device), zeroed once and reset to 0 by the last-ticket program, so it holds nothing derived from data. _inv_freq is keyed on config theta. Both are fine. Make sure _counters' torch.zeros runs on the eager warm-up call, not inside graph capture; it did in the earlier passing run, and the port is verbatim.

Every key: the old-key chunking covers [max(0, seq - 2047), seq - 1] across S=16 splits (chunk rounded up to BLOCK_N=64, 16*128 >= 2047), plus the new key from registers. All 2048 window keys are scored, with no skipping.
No host syncs. The branch reads cfg['window'], cfg['batch'] and cfg['q_len'] only. The workspace is fresh torch.empty of fixed config shapes each call.

The only test that reaches the gated path is 'batch 1, ctx 10, heads tp8, layer sliding' (page_size 64 by default; PAGE is a constexpr, and most splits are empty with m = -inf, which gets weight 0). It passed before.
open_questions: Has fa3-window-trimmed-page-table harvested, and did it move sliding decode_1? If it did, recompute the expected margin against the new master's decode_1 sliding row before claiming, and consider holding if trimmed FA3 comes within about 1 us of 13.5.
Was the earlier 13.51 us measured under identical judge and evaluator versions? Compare evaluator_sha256 with bfb7bac's run.

If classify() calls it neutral only on CI overlap, the reviewer's acceptance rule is the per-shape test: sliding decode_1 at least about 10% faster with the other 11 rows within drift, the same reasoning used to merge batch-gate by hand.
With 5 attention checks left today, this costs one check at a single-shape prediction of about 18%. Decide whether it ranks above the pending reruns.
